claims.basis: PMR identifies the exact car as BMW V12 LMR and the model's documented history identifies its 1999 debut and six-speed sequential Xtrac transmission.

Both sources specify six forward speeds. Sequential manual is established; the reviewed sources do not explicitly document paddle actuation, so the conservative proposal is a sequential stick. The transmission is explicitly sequential. Downshift-only action. Modeled only for upshifts. The documented sequential manual racing transmission is not described as an automated launch system; a clutch is required to launch under the project's derivation rules. Reinspection of the supplied full cockpit photographs shows a D-shaped/flattened steering-wheel profile, not a circular rim. The images appear to depict the same later display/restored cockpit configuration, so this is a cautious photographed-configuration finding rather than two independent period confirmations. The visible wheel face contains spokes and controls but no integrated screen; the instruments are mounted on the dashboard behind the wheel. This is a direct observation of the supplied photographs. No rim-mounted shift-light strip or lamps are visible on the fully exposed wheel face in the supplied photographs; dashboard indicators are not counted as wheel shift lights. The photographed rim forms a continuous closed circumference rather than an open-top wheel. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/gearbox_type, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip.
